```js
// Sixty circles drifting on individual noise paths over a dark ground.
// Each keeps its own offsets into the noise field so the flock never
// moves as one body, which is what makes the drift read as drift.

let circles = [];
const COUNT = 60;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(windowWidth, windowHeight);
  noStroke();
  for (let i = 0; i < COUNT; i++) {
    circles.push({
      x: random(width),
      y: random(height),
      r: random(8, 26),
      xoff: random(1000),
      yoff: random(1000),
      vx: 0,
      vy: 0
    });
  }
}

function draw() {
  background(12, 14, 20);
  for (const c of circles) {
    // Noise supplies the wander; velocity supplies the memory of a click.
    c.x += (noise(c.xoff) - 0.5) * 2.4 + c.vx;
    c.y += (noise(c.yoff) - 0.5) * 2.4 + c.vy;
    c.xoff += 0.006;
    c.yoff += 0.006;
    c.vx *= 0.94;
    c.vy *= 0.94;
    c.x = (c.x + width) % width;
    c.y = (c.y + height) % height;
    fill(255, 170, 90, 190);
    circle(c.x, c.y, c.r * 2);
  }
}

function mousePressed() {
  for (const c of circles) {
    const d = max(dist(mouseX, mouseY, c.x, c.y), 1);
    const push = 900 / d;
    c.vx += ((c.x - mouseX) / d) * push;
    c.vy += ((c.y - mouseY) / d) * push;
  }
}

function windowResized() {
  resizeCanvas(windowWidth, windowHeight);
}
```

## Statement

Sixty small suns wander a night field, each on its own private path through a
noise landscape, so the group never quite agrees on a direction. A click is a
shove: everything near the cursor is thrown outward at once and then, as the
damping takes hold, forgets it and returns to drifting. I wanted the recovery to
be the subject rather than the scatter — the piece is about how quickly a crowd
goes back to what it was doing.
